'''Étienne Fouvry''' ({{IPA|fr|etjɛn fuvʁi}}, born 1953<ref name=idref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idref.fr/083861688|title=Fouvry, Étienne (1953–)|work=IdRef|access-date=2024-07-10}}</ref>) is a French mathematician working primarily in [[analytic number theory]].<ref name=hunting/>

Fouvry defended his dissertation in 1981 at the [[University of Bordeaux]] under the joint direction of [[Henryk Iwaniec]] and [[Jean-Marc Deshouillers]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|70016}}</ref> He is an emeritus professor at [[Paris-Saclay University]] and the 2021 recipient of the [[Sophie Germain Prize]].<ref name=hunting>{{cite web|url=https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/en/news/etienne-fouvry-hunting-prime-numbers|title=Étienne Fouvry: Hunting for prime numbers|publisher=Paris-Saclay University|date=4 February 2022|access-date=2024-06-12}}</ref>

In 1985, Fouvry showed that the first case of [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] is true for infinitely many primes.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Fouvry | first=Étienne | journal=[[Invent. Math.]] | title=Théorème de Brun-Titchmarsh: application au théorème de Fermat | language=fr | trans-title=The Brun-Titchmarsh theorem: application to the Fermat theorem | volume=79 | issue=2 | year=1985 | pages=383–407 | mr=0778134 | doi=10.1007/BF01388980| bibcode=1985InMat..79..383F | s2cid=122719070 }}</ref>
